war.d: Organized, large-scale, armed conflict between countries or between national, ethnic, or other sizeable groups, usually but not always involving active engagement of military forces.(Can we clean up this sense?)
war.e: War is merely the continuation of policy by other means;   War is hell

warm.d: Having a temperature slightly higher than usual, but still pleasant; mildly hot.

was.d: first-person singular simple past indicative of be.

wash.d: The process or an instance of washing or being washed by water or other liquid.
wash.e: I'm going to have a quick wash before coming to bed.

watch.e: More people today carry a watch on their wrists than in their pockets.

water.d: A substance (of molecular formula H₂O) found at room temperature and pressure as a clear liquid; it is present naturally as rain, and found in rivers, lakes and seas; its solid form is ice and its gaseous form is steam.
water.e: By the action of electricity, the water was resolved into its two parts, oxygen and hydrogen.

way.d: (heading) To do with a place or places.
way.e: You're going about it the wrong way.  He's known for his quirky ways.  I don't like the way she looks at me.

we.d: (personal) The speakers/writers, or the speaker/writer and at least one other person (not the person being addressed). (This is the exclusive we.)

wear.d: To have on: To carry or have equipped on or about one's body, as an item of clothing, equipment, decoration, perfume, etc.

weather.d: The short term state of the atmosphere at a specific time and place, including the temperature, relative humidity, cloud cover, precipitation, wind, etc.
weather.e: Wooden garden furniture must be well oiled as it is continuously exposed to weather.

week.d: Any period of seven consecutive days.

weekend.d: The break in the working week, usually two days including the traditional holy or sabbath day. Thus in western countries, Saturday and Sunday.

well.e: I had been sick, but now I'm well.

were.d: second-person singular simple past indicative of be
were.e: John, you were the only person to see him.

what.d: (Singlish) Used to contradict an underlying assumption held by the interlocutor.
what.e: The market will calculate these higher risks in their funding costs what might result in higher lending rates.

wheel.d: A circular device capable of rotating on its axis, facilitating movement or transportation or performing labour in machines.
wheel.e: Wheel that trolley over here, would you?

when.d: The time at which something happens.
when.e: A good article will cover the who, the what, the when, the where, the why and the how.

where.d: The place in which something happens.
where.e: A good article will cover the who, the what, the when, the where, the why and the how.

which.d: (interrogative) What one or ones (of those mentioned or implied).
which.e: By now, you must surely know which is which.

who.d: A person under discussion; a question of which person.
who.e: I don't know who it is. (indirect question)

whose.d: Of whom, belonging to whom; which person's or people's.

why.e: A good article will cover the who, the what, the when, the where, the why and the how.

wife.d: A married woman, especially in relation to her spouse.

wind.d: Real or perceived movement of atmospheric air usually caused by convection or differences in air pressure.
wind.e: As they accelerated onto the motorway, the wind tore the plywood off the car's roof-rack.

window.d: An opening, usually covered by one or more panes of clear glass, to allow light and air from outside to enter a building or vehicle.
window.e: She opened the window to let some air in.

winter.d: Traditionally the fourth of the four seasons, typically regarded as spanning either the period between the winter solstice to the spring equinox, or the months of December, January, and February in temperate and polar regions of the Northern Hemisphere and the months of June, July, and August in the Southern Hemisphere. It is the time when the sun is lowest in the sky, resulting in short days, and the time of year with the lowest atmospheric temperatures for the region.

wish.d: A desire, hope, or longing for something or for something to happen.
wish.e: It is my wish that the bequest (should) be given to an almshouse.

with.d: Along, together with others, in a group, etc.
with.e: Do you want to come with?

wonderful.d: Tending to excite wonder; surprising, extraordinary.
wonderful.e: His delusion was not wonderful, but most natural.

word.d: The smallest unit of language that has a particular meaning and can be expressed by itself; the smallest discrete, meaningful unit of language. (contrast morpheme.)
word.e: I’m not sure how to word this letter to the council.

worker.d: One who works: a person who performs labor for a living; traditionally, especially, manual labor.

world.d: (with "the") Human collective existence; existence in general.
world.e: There will always be lovers, till the world’s end.

worry.d: To be troubled; to give way to mental anxiety or doubt.
worry.e: I'm afflicted by worry throughout the night.

would.d: Past tense of will; usually followed by a bare infinitive. Used to form the "anterior future", or "future in the past", indicating a futurity relative to a past time.
would.e: On my first day at University, I met the woman who would become my wife.

write.d: To form letters, words or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.
write.e: The pupil wrote his name on the paper.

writer.d: A person who writes, or produces literary work.
writer.e: Has your girlfriend written you another letter already? She’s quite a writer!

wrong.d: Something that is immoral or not good.

yellow.d: The colour of gold, butter, or a lemon; the colour obtained by mixing green and red light, or by subtracting blue from white light.

yes.d: An affirmative expression; an answer that shows agreement or acceptance.

yesterday.d: The day immediately before today; one day ago.
yesterday.e: Today is the child of yesterday and the parent of tomorrow.

yet.d: (usually with negative) Thus far; up to the present; up to some specified time; still
yet.e: He has never yet been late for an appointment;   I’m not yet wise enough to answer that;   Have you finished yet?

you.d: To address (a person) using the pronoun you (in the past, especially to use you rather than thou, when you was considered more formal).
you.e: Both of you should get ready now.

yours.d: That or those belonging to you; the possessive second-person singular pronoun used without a following noun.
yours.e: If this edit is mine, the other must be yours.

yourself.e: Be careful with that fire or you'll burn yourself.

zoo.d: A park where live animals are exhibited.
zoo.e: The London Zoo was built in 1828.
